# Parley v0.1.43

Four changes from the acceptance pass on v0.1.42, all about teams: the Work
list shows the session's own work, stopped team panes can be closed together,
a Claude host member no longer asks before Parley's own commands, and the app
says plainly that a host team is supervised automation.

## The Work list shows only the session's work

The Team Sessions sheet listed every handoff the requesting pane had ever
made, with anyone, under "Work". Every acceptance run reported it. A session's
work is now exactly the handoffs with a session-created pane on either side,
started after that pane existed and not after the session ended. The
requester's other handoffs, before or during the session, are not listed, and
the decisions list follows the same rule.

## Close stopped team panes together

After a session stops, its panes stay as stopped placeholders and the
workspace fills up. The sheet now offers **Close stopped team panes…**, which
names each placeholder in one confirmation and closes only those. Ownership is
re-read after you confirm: a pane you restarted since, the requester,
unrelated panes and the last pane of a workspace are never closed here, and
anything skipped is reported.

## Claude runs `parley` commands without asking

A Claude host pane on a profile that allows shell execution still asked before
every `parley` command, because acceptEdits mode only pre-approves file edits.
Parley's generated Claude settings now carry allow rules for its own command,
`Bash(parley:*)` and the runtime-local shim path, the counterpart of the
`shell(parley)` permission Copilot already had. Every other shell command
keeps Claude's prompt. A profile that asks before shell commands keeps asking
for `parley` too, because that was your choice.

Verified in two real Claude sessions driven in a terminal, identical except
for the rule: with it, `parley whoami` ran with no prompt; without it, Claude
prompted and nothing ran.

## A host team is supervised automation

Help, the team approval text and the agent protocol now say what a host team
can and cannot do unattended: Claude runs `parley` commands without asking but
asks before other shell commands, Codex asks when a command needs to leave its
sandbox, and Agy asks before commands and offers no allowlist, only a
skip-all-permissions flag that Parley never passes on the host. Only container
members whose bypass you approved run without prompts. Plan an unattended
team around those.

## Also

- Recipes now ask for progress notes at milestones of work longer than a
  minute or so, and the protocol says a ten-second check needs none.
- `docs/test-scenarios.md` P3.3 gains the Work-list, grouped-close and
  Claude-prompt expectations.

## Compatibility

Agent protocol semantics are unchanged and the version stays at 32; the
protocol text gains guidance sentences only. Existing Claude panes pick up the
allow rules on their next start or restart. No stored record changes shape.

Validated: 343 native checks, 53 Node tests, public scan, platform scan and
build. The Work-list check was watched failing under the old any-participant
rule and passing under the new one. The Claude rule was proved in real
sessions as described above. Not driven by hand: the grouped close in the
running app; it is the P3.3 step to try first.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
